summary.text: Teresa Pierce is the Democratic majority leader of the Maine Senate, representing District 25, and is running for re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election.
She served in the Maine House of Representatives from 2014 to 2022 and previously served on the Falmouth Town Council.

paragraphs.text: Teresa Pierce lives in Falmouth, Maine, and earned a B.A. in political science and public policy from the University of Colorado at Boulder in 1985.

She served on the Falmouth Town Council for six years, including two years as its chair, and worked as associate director of alumni advancement at the University of New England and for other nonprofit organizations.
Pierce was first elected to the Maine House in 2014, defeating Republican Gregory Payeur, 48.9% to 46%, in the general election for District 44, and was re-elected in 2016, 2018 and 2020.

In 2016 and 2017 she was House chair of the Joint Select Committee on Marijuana Legalization Implementation, and in the 2021–2022 session she chaired the Appropriations and Financial Affairs Committee.
She was elected Senate majority leader in November 2024.
In the 2025–2026 session she chairs the Senate Rules Committee and the Senatorial Vote Committee and serves on the Education and Cultural Affairs and Transportation committees.
